'''Julia A. Kovacs''' is an American chemist specializing in [[bioinorganic chemistry]]. She is professor of chemistry at the [[University of Washington]]. Her research involves synthesizing [[Small molecule|small-molecule]] mimics of the active sites of [[metalloprotein]]s, in order to investigate how [[Cysteine|cysteinates]] influence the function of [[Non-heme iron protein|non-heme iron enzymes]], and the mechanism of the [[Oxygen-evolving complex|oxygen-evolving complex (OEC)]].

== Early life and education ==
Kovacs completed her undergraduate degree at [[Michigan State University]], graduating with a B.S. in chemistry in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chem.umn.edu/event/department-seminar-professor-julie-kovacs|title=Department Seminar: Professor Julie A. Kovacs|last=harva015|date=2019-09-12|website=Department of Chemistry|language=en|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> There, she worked with Prof. Bruce Averill on the synthesis of [[Iron–sulfur cluster|iron-sulfur cluster]] compounds, which mimic the [[FeMoco|FeMo-cofactor]] of [[nitrogenase]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1986-01-01|title=Synthesis of a new class of Mo-Fe-S clusters containing the MoS2Fe2 unit|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277538700849396|journal=Polyhedron|language=en|volume=5|issue=1–2|pages=393–398|doi=10.1016/S0277-5387(00)84939-6|issn=0277-5387|last1=Bose |first1=K.S. |last2=Lamberty |first2=P.E. |last3=Kovacs |first3=J.E. |last4=Sinn |first4=E. |last5=Averill |first5=B.A. |url-access=subscription}}</ref> She then moved to [[Harvard University]] for graduate studies, and there she continued her work on iron-sulfur clusters with Prof. [[Richard H. Holm]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kovacs|first1=Julie A.|last2=Bashkin|first2=J. K.|last3=Holm|first3=R. H.|date=March 1985|title=Persulfide-bridged iron-molybdenum-sulfur clusters of biological relevance: two synthetic routes and the structures of intermediate and product clusters|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ja00292a067|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=107|issue=6|pages=1784–1786|doi=10.1021/ja00292a067|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kovacs|first1=Julie A.|last2=Holm|first2=R. H.|date=1986-01-01|title=Assembly of vanadium-iron-sulfur cubane clusters from mononuclear and linear trinuclear reactants|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00262a050|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=108|issue=2|pages=340–341|doi=10.1021/ja00262a050|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kovacs|first1=Julie A.|last2=Holm|first2=Richard H.|date=March 1987|title=Heterometallic clusters: synthesis and reactions of vanadium-iron-sulfur single- and double-cubane clusters and the structure of [V2Fe6S8Cl4(C2H4S2)2]4-|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ic00252a014|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=26|issue=5|pages=702–711|doi=10.1021/ic00252a014|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kovacs|first1=Julie A.|last2=Holm|first2=Richard H.|date=March 1987|title=Structural chemistry of vanadium-iron-sulfur clusters containing the cubane-type [VFe3S4]2+ core|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ic00252a015|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=26|issue=5|pages=711–718|doi=10.1021/ic00252a015|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1987-01-01|title=[Fe2S2(CO)6]2− as a cluster precursor: synthesis and structure of [MoFe3S6(CO)6]2− and oxidative decarbonylation to a persulfide-bridged MoFe3S4 double cubane|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0277538700809080|journal=Polyhedron|language=en|volume=6|issue=6|pages=1445–1456|doi=10.1016/S0277-5387(00)80908-0|issn=0277-5387|last1=Kovacs |first1=Julie A. |last2=Bashkin |first2=James K. |last3=Holm |first3=R.H. |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Kovacs graduated with her PhD in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://depts.washington.edu/kovaclab/kovacslab/group.html|title=Kovacs Lab Members|website=depts.washington.edu|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> She then moved to California to conduct postdoctoral research at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where she worked with Prof. [[Robert G. == Research and career ==
Kovacs began her independent research career in 1988 when she joined the [[University of Washington]] as an assistant professor. She was promoted to associate professor in 1994, then further promoted to full professor in 2001. She was chair of the [[American Chemical Society]] Division of Inorganic Chemistry in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Julie Kovacs elected Chair of the ACS Division of Inorganic Chemistry {{!}} Department of Chemistry {{!}} University of Washington|url=https://chem.washington.edu/news/2019/04/18/julie-kovacs-elected-chair-acs-division-inorganic-chemistry|access-date=2021-05-17|website=chem.washington.edu}}</ref>

Kovacs' research involves investigations into the role of thiolates in dioxygen chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kovacs|first=Julie A.|date=2003-02-14|title=How Iron Activates O2|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1081792|journal=Science|language=en|volume=299|issue=5609|pages=1024–1025|doi=10.1126/science.1081792|issn=0036-8075|pmid=12586930|s2cid=93705834|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Non-heme iron protein|Non-heme iron enzymes]] are known to promote biological reactions, but the mechanisms by which [[Cysteine|cysteinates]] impact their function are not well understood.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shearer|first1=Jason|last2=Scarrow|first2=Robert C.|last3=Kovacs|first3=Julie A.|date=2002-10-01|title=Synthetic Models for the Cysteinate-Ligated Non-Heme Iron Enzyme Superoxide Reductase: Observation and Structural Characterization by XAS of an FeIII−OOH Intermediate|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=124|issue=39|pages=11709–11717|doi=10.1021/ja012722b|pmid=12296737|issn=0002-7863}}</ref>

Kovacs is interested in the formation of the oxygen–oxygen bond.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Kovacs Lab Research|url=http://depts.washington.edu/kovaclab/kovacslab/research.html|access-date=2020-03-09|website=depts.washington.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1664682&HistoricalAwards=false|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1664682 - Understanding the Mechanism of Mn-Promoted H2O Oxidation|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref> In nature, it is this [[oxygen-evolving complex]] (OEC) that stores solar energy in chemical bonds. By creating a series of small molecule analogues, Kovacs studies the radical coupling mechanism by which Mn<sup>IV</sup>-oxyl radicals attach bridging oxo groups. She also investigates nucleophilic attack of Mn<sup>V</sup>-oxo due to hydroxyl groups on the OEC. The small molecules include nitrogen and sulphur and a particular [[stereochemistry]]. Through synthesis of organic molecules with a variety of different molecular frameworks, Kovacs investigates their structure-property relationships and the reactivity of the resulting transition-metal complexes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://depts.washington.edu/chem/people/faculty/kovacs.html|title=Julie A. Kovacs - UW Dept. of Chemistry|website=depts.washington.edu|access-date=2020-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yan Poon|first1=Penny Chaau|last2=Dedushko|first2=Maksym === Selected publications ===
Her publications include:

* Synthetic analogues of cysteinate-ligated non-heme iron and non-corrinoid cobalt enzymes ([[doi:10.1021/cr020619e|DOI: 10.1021/cr020619e]])<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kovacs|first=Julie A.|date=2004-05-25|title=Synthetic Analogues of Cysteinate-Ligated Non-Heme Iron and Non-Corrinoid Cobalt Enzymes|journal=ChemInform|volume=35|issue=21|pages=825–848|doi=10.1002/chin.200421278|pmid=14871143|issn=0931-7597|pmc=4487544}}</ref>
* Synthetic Models for the Cysteinate-Ligated Non-Heme Iron Enzyme [[Superoxide reductase|Superoxide Reductase]]:  Observation and Structural Characterization by XAS of an Fe<sup>III</sup>−OOH Intermediate ([[doi:10.1021/ja012722b|DOI: 10.1021/ja012722b]])<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shearer|first1=Jason|last2=Scarrow|first2=Robert C.|last3=Kovacs|first3=Julie A.|date=2002|title=Synthetic Models for the Cysteinate-Ligated Non-Heme Iron Enzyme Superoxide Reductase: Observation and Structural Characterization by XAS of an Fe III −OOH Intermediate|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=124|issue=39|pages=11709–11717|doi=10.1021/ja012722b|pmid=12296737|issn=0002-7863}}</ref>
* Understanding how the thiolate sulfur contributes to the function of the non-heme iron enzyme superoxide reductase ([[doi:10.1021/ar600059h|DOI: 10.1021/ar600059h]])<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kovacs|first1=Julie A.|last2=Brines|first2=Lisa M.|date=2007-10-02|title=Understanding How the Thiolate Sulfur Contributes to the Function of the Non-Heme Iron Enzyme Superoxide Reductase|journal=ChemInform|volume=38|issue=40|pages=501–509|doi=10.1002/chin.200740273|pmid=17536780|issn=0931-7597|pmc=3703784}}</ref>
